Hays Brisbane | Public Sector Project Engineer    Your new company     
 Join a large local government organisation supporting the delivery of essential civil infrastructure projects across the Brisbane region. You will be part of a busy construction team responsible for delivering projects safely, efficiently and in line with agreed budgets, timeframes and quality standards. 
   Your new role     
 As a Project Engineer, you will assist with the delivery of assigned civil construction projects and programs of work. You will work closely with Construction and Delivery Managers to support project planning, procurement, contractor management, risk management and technical delivery. 
 Your responsibilities will include managing project costs, monitoring schedules, supporting procurement and contract delivery, providing technical advice, coordinating quality assurance processes and ensuring projects are delivered to scope, budget and safety requirements. 
 This is a contract opportunity until 25 June 2027, based from Carina Heights with work across various project locations. 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Tertiary qualification in Engineering. 
 Current C Class driver's licence. 
 Current White Card or equivalent construction safety competency. 
 Strong technical knowledge in civil engineering, construction management and procurement. 
 Experience delivering and managing civil construction projects. 
 Ability to apply WHS, environmental and quality policies in an operational field environment. 
 Experience using Microsoft Project, SAP, works management systems and general office software. 
 Strong communication skills with the ability to liaise with technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 
   What you'll get in return     
 
 Contract opportunity through to June 2027. 
 5 x 8-hour days, with a maximum 40-hour work week. 
 Opportunity to work on civil construction projects that support essential community infrastructure. 
 Exposure to project delivery, procurement, contractor management and quality assurance. 
 Work within a supportive construction team across varied project sites. 
 Depot based at Carina Heights with work across various locations. 
 
   What you need to do now     
 If you're interested in this role, forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call now. 
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact Chall Tehuia on 07 3243 3079 for a confidential discussion on your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

Job Description:
The Analyst Programmer is responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining software applications that support business objectives. Key duties include writing and reviewing code, conducting software testing, and ensuring that application functionality meets specified requirements. The role also involves researching and designing technical solutions, as well as documenting and updating software specifications throughout the development lifecycle.
Responsibilities:
Demonstrate a strong understanding of coding methods, industry best practices, and software development standards.
Conduct interviews with end-users to gather insights into functionality, interface issues, usability, and challenges, ensuring user needs are effectively addressed.
Develop comprehensive test cases and test plans to ensure the reliability and performance of software applications.
Stay informed on data privacy laws and practices to ensure software development remains compliant.
Communicate clearly with non-technical staff and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
Embrace new technologies and maintain a commitment to ongoing learning and skill development.
Display excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills to convey ideas and requirements effectively.
Conduct research into software-related challenges and assess potential solutions or products.
Demonstrate initiative, autonomy, and direction in executing work tasks and delivering projects.
Maintain strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy and precision throughout the development process.
Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to resolve complex software-related issues.
Manage task prioritisation and execute effectively under pressure to meet project deadlines.
Collaborate closely with developers, programmers, and designers to conceptualise and develop innovative software solutions.
Evaluate existing business systems and processes to identify optimisation opportunities.
Assist in gathering, defining, and documenting business requirements, deliverables, and specifications in partnership with internal departments.
Contribute to software development project planning, including scope definition, scheduling, and implementation.
Engage with internal and external programme users to understand and fulfil functional requirements.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
At least 2 years of hands-on experience working as an Analyst Programmer or in a similar software development role.
Proficient in one or more programming languages such as Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript.
Strong understanding of database concepts and practical experience writing and optimising SQL queries.
Experience developing web applications using technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Angular, or ASP.NET.
Familiarity with modern software development methodologies, including Agile and Scrum frameworks.
Sound knowledge of software testing principles, with exposure to tools like JUnit or Selenium.
Experience using version control systems such as Git or SVN, and project tracking tools like JIRA or Trello.
Understanding of cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, along with their core services and deployment models.
Solid foundation in object-oriented programming (OOP) and commonly used software design patterns.
Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to identify and resolve complex coding issues.
Effective communicator with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to manage tasks, prioritise deliverables, and meet project deadlines.
Self-motivated with a commitment to ongoing learning and staying current with emerging tools and technologies.
Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Types: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super
Benefits: Work from home
Schedule: 8-hour shift
Work Authorisation: Australia (Required)

Position  : Full Time 
Location : Goulburn NSW

Hidrive designs, manufactures and installs light, strong, fit-for-purpose service bodies for utes, trailers, and trucks — trusted by trades, industry and governments since 1993. Hidrive is Australia’s only service body manufacturer with a company-owned national installation network, and it designs, builds and installs fit-for-purpose service bodies for all trades and industries at our company-owned facilities in Adelaide, Brisbane, Goulburn, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney.

Hidrive is currently looking for hardworking and dedicated Press Brake Operator to join their team.
  
The Press Brake Operator is responsible for setting up and operating CNC press brake machinery to bend, form, and fabricate sheet metal components in accordance with engineering drawings and production specifications. The role ensures products are manufactured accurately, efficiently, and to the required quality standards while maintaining a safe working environment.

Key Responsibilities
Set up and operate CNC press brakes
Program and operate press brakes, when necessary, not mandatory
Select correct tooling and develop bend sequences
Read and interpret engineering drawings
Perform first-off and in-process quality checks
Maintain productivity and quality standards during night shift
Troubleshoot bending issues and adjust programs where required
Maintain a clean and safe workspace

Skills & Experience
At least 2 years of relevant experience 
Relevant qualification
Proven experience as a Press Brake Operator
Experience working with CNC press brake machines
Ability to work independently without supervision
Strong sheet metal fabrication knowledge
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings
High attention to detail and quality


If you think you have got the skills and experience to join our team, please apply now. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

result.description:
Who We Are
We're a proud Tasmanian family-owned business with over a century of experience in general engineering. Our modern fabrication and machining workshops are located just 10 minutes south of Hobart in Kingston. We specialise in the manufacture, repair, refurbishment, installation, and maintenance of industrial equipment.

The Opportunity
We're on the lookout for skilled Boilermaker Welders to join our dynamic team. Our workshop operations cover a wide range of fabrication and welding tasks, from light to heavy work with steel, stainless steel and aluminium components. You'll work from engineering drawings and use equipment such as CNC plasma cutters, plate rolls, brake presses, bandsaws, and various welding techniques such as MIG, TIG and stick.

What You'll Do
Operate equipment such as plate rolls, rotators, bandsaws, presses and overhead cranes.
Use a variety of welding equipment including MIG, TIG, and stick.
Fabricate steel, aluminium, and stainless-steel components and assemblies.
Carryout repairs on plant and equipment.
Perform welding tasks that range from basic general-purpose applications to coded welding on quality-critical components and equipment.

Why Join Us?
At Saunders & Ward, we offer:
The option to work a 4-day week.
Excellent working conditions.
Stable employment with a well-established, family-owned company.
A diverse range of stimulating work.
Modern, well-organised and clean workshops.
A friendly, safety-focused culture.
Regular overtime.
A graded pay structure that rewards skills and experience.
Annual performance and wage reviews.
Rostered days off (RDOs).

What We're Looking For
To be successful in this role, you should have:
A strong commitment to safe work practices.
A fabrication trade qualification.
Engineering workshop experience.
Experience with mild steel MIG welding and fabrication.
The ability to complete jobs on time and to quality standards.
The ability to pass drug and alcohol screening.

If you're ready to bring your skills and experience to a great team, we'd love to hear from you! Please submit your cover letter and resume to our Fabrication Manager, Matt Brown, via our online application.

result.description: Mansys Pty Ltd   Electrical Engineering Technician    Employer:  Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd   Location:  Brendale, Queensland 4500   Position:  Full-time   Salary:  AUD 80,000 to A$90,000 per annum plus superannuation, commensurate with skills and experience       Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled and experienced Electrical Engineering Technician to join their team in Brendale, Queensland. The successful candidate will support the design, manufacture, testing, commissioning and quality checking of low-voltage electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres and control panels.  This role is suited to a technically competent person with experience in electrical systems, switchboard manufacture, testing procedures, technical drawings, electrical components and Australian electrical standards.   Key duties and responsibilities   The Electrical Engineering Technician will be responsible for:   Assisting Electrical Engineers, project managers and senior technical staff with the design and layout of electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres, control panels, cabling arrangements and associated electrical systems.  Preparing, interpreting and reviewing technical drawings, wiring diagrams, layout drawings, schematics and electrical plans for switchboard manufacturing projects.  Conducting tests on electrical systems, components and switchboard assemblies to confirm operational performance, safety and compliance with project specifications.  Collecting technical data, recording test results, performing calculations, preparing test documentation, charts, reports and tabulations for engineering and quality assurance purposes.  Assisting with estimating material requirements, component quantities, labour requirements and project costs for switchboard and electrical assembly works.  Inspecting designs, manufactured switchboards and completed electrical assemblies to ensure compliance with specifications, Australian Standards, client requirements and safety requirements.  Assembling, installing, testing, calibrating, modifying and repairing electrical equipment, switchboard components, protection devices, metering equipment, indicating devices and control equipment.  Supporting workshop electrical functions, including installation of assemblies for protection relays, metering devices, control circuits and electrical indicating equipment.  Assisting with fault finding, technical problem solving and rectification of electrical issues during manufacture, testing and commissioning.  Liaising with internal design, fabrication, assembly and project teams to ensure switchboards are delivered accurately, safely and on time.  Maintaining accurate technical records, testing records, compliance documents and quality assurance documentation.  Ensuring all work is performed in accordance with workplace health and safety requirements, company procedures, project specifications and relevant Australian Standards.    Skills and experience required   Applicants must have:   Diploma or Bachelors in Electrical Engineering or related field  Atleast 2 years of experience in electrical switchboard manufacture, electrical systems, control panels, distribution boards, motor control centres or similar electrical engineering environments.  Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics and technical specifications.  Experience conducting electrical tests, recording results and assisting with technical reporting.  Knowledge of electrical components such as circuit breakers, busbars, contactors, relays, metering equipment, control devices, terminals and cabling systems.    Skills Required    Good technical problem-solving skills and strong attention to detail.  Ability to work safely and effectively in a workshop/manufacturing environment.  Good communication skills and ability to work as part of a technical project team.      Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
